tex_content.label: introclaim5
tex_content.html:
There is a finite collection $\{ (H_i,x_i)\} _{i=1}^k$ of complete pointed finite-volume $3$-manifolds with constant sectional curvature $-1/4$ and, for large $t$, a decreasing function $\alpha (t)\ra 0$ and maps \begin{equation} f_t\: :\bigsqcup _{i=1}^kH_i\: \supset \: \bigsqcup _{i=1}^k B\left(x_i,\frac{1}{\alpha (t)}\right)\longrightarrow M_t \end{equation} such that 1. $f_t$ is $\alpha (t)$-close to an isometry; 2. the image of $f_t$ contains $M^+(\alpha (t),t)$; 3. the image under $f_t$ of every cuspidal torus of $\{ H_i\} _{i=1}^k$ is incompressible in $M_t$.

The proof of Claim 2 uses Hamilton's earlier work \cite{Hamiltonn}.
